channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan President begins official visit to Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Belgrade for an official visit. He was met by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić. The visit includes high-level Uzbek-Serbian negotiations and a business forum, with a package of bilateral documents expected to be signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Higher Education System Undergoing Major Reforms and Expansion
item.description: Uzbekistan's higher education system is undergoing significant transformation, with a focus on accessibility, quality, and scientific potential. The number of higher education institutions has grown from 77 to 205 in ten years, and student enrollment has tripled. Private sector involvement has led to the establishment of 74 non-state universities.

item.title: Tashkent prepares for autumn-winter season with focus on utility readiness
item.description: Tashkent held a working meeting to prepare the city for the autumn-winter period, ensuring safe and uninterrupted operation. Participants focused on the readiness of utility services and public service systems for increased seasonal loads. Measures to ensure resident safety during cold weather, including fire and carbon monoxide poisoning prevention, were also discussed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's beef imports rose 23% in August; new train route launched
item.description: Uzbekistan's beef imports increased by 23% in August. The number of citizens emigrating from Uzbekistan decreased. President Mirziyoyev ordered strict adherence to liquefied gas supply schedules. New electric trains will operate on the Khiva-Bukhara route.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imports Less but More Expensive Gasoline, Analyzing Import Trends and Prices
item.description: From January to August, Uzbekistan imported 721.5 million liters of gasoline, a 41.2% increase year-on-year. The import value rose by 48.6% to $437.4 million. The average import price per 1,000 liters increased by 5.3% to $606, with a significant surge in August reaching nearly $995.

item.title: Filmmaker Aybek Daiyrbekov appointed Deputy Minister of Culture in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Filmmaker, screenwriter, and producer Aybek Daiyrbekov has been appointed Deputy Minister of Culture, Information, and Youth Policy in Kyrgyzstan. The decision was signed by Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. Daiyrbekov is a recipient of the Honored Cultural Worker of the Kyrgyz Republic title.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrives in Serbia for official visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Serbia for an official visit. He was welcomed at the Nikola Tesla International Airport by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić and his wife.

item.title: Russia and North Korea inaugurate first border bridge over Tumen River
item.description: Russia and North Korea have officially opened a new automobile bridge across the Tumen River, connecting the two countries. The bridge, named after Soviet officer Yakov Novichenko, replaces the sole existing railway bridge.

item.title: Chinese electric train service to launch between Khiva and Bukhara on September 9
item.description: A Chinese-made CR200J electric train will begin operating between Khiva and Bukhara starting September 9, according to Uzbekistan Railways. The service will extend from Urgench Airport to the Bukhara-1 station, running six days a week.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Identify Promising Areas for Digitalization Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia held a roundtable on digital transformation, focusing on cooperation in digital technologies, artificial intelligence, and the digital economy. Participants discussed expanding the use of these technologies in the economy, social sphere, and government. The initiative to form a joint digital ecosystem between the two countries was highlighted.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan Departs for Official Visit to Belgrade
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, has departed for Serbia on an official visit at the invitation of President Aleksandar Vučić. The program includes high-level negotiations and a business forum. Discussions will focus on strengthening multifaceted Uzbek-Serbian cooperation, with a package of documents expected to be signed.

item.title: Bishkek city hall reviews post-SCO and VIK summit tasks for urban services
item.description: Bishkek city hall has reviewed the outcomes of major international events hosted in the capital and outlined future tasks for city services and district administrations. The mayor emphasized the need for continued infrastructure development, including road and facade renovations, and ordered an audit of expenses to ensure targeted fund utilization and quality control.

item.title: Bishkek Mayor's Office reviews post-SCO summit tasks for city services
item.description: The Bishkek Mayor's Office has summarized the outcomes of major international events held in the capital and outlined future tasks for city services and district administrations. The mayor emphasized the need for continued infrastructure development, including road and sidewalk repairs, facade renovations, and landscaping, with a focus on auditing expenses and ensuring quality.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ranks 61st in Global Peace Index
item.description: Kyrgyzstan secured 61st place out of 163 countries in the Global Peace Index 2026. The country scored 1.853 points, according to the Institute for Economics & Peace. Neighboring countries also ranked: Kazakhstan (44th), Tajikistan (47th), Uzbekistan (37th), and Turkmenistan (66th).

item.title: Responsibility for Nuclear Safety Violations to Be Strengthened in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's legislative chamber discussed amendments to laws concerning industrial, radiation, and nuclear safety. The proposed changes aim to improve state supervision, align with international standards, and strengthen measures to prevent violations. The bill clarifies the powers of the Committee for Industrial, Radiation, and Nuclear Safety and the Inspectorate for Mining and Geological Supervision.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Loans to individuals approach 240 trillion soums, with mortgages leading
item.description: As of August 1, 2026, outstanding loans to individuals in Uzbekistan reached nearly 240 trillion soums, an 8.9% increase since the start of the year. Mortgages constitute the largest share at 36.8%, totaling 88.1 trillion soums. Microloans follow, with an outstanding balance of 51.1 trillion soums.

item.title: Israel Launches New Strikes on Lebanon, Killing 11
item.description: Israel conducted further strikes on Lebanon, resulting in 11 fatalities. Lebanon reported that the strikes by Israeli forces were carried out without prior online evacuation warnings to the civilian population.

item.title: Turkmenistan elected chair of Landlocked Developing Countries Group for 2027-2028
item.description: Turkmenistan has been elected as the chair of the Group of Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDCs) for the 2027-2028 period. Azerbaijan will serve as vice-chair. This position will allow Turkmenistan to coordinate the group's activities, representing 32 developing nations, in areas like energy and transport.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China expand cooperation in environmental education and green talent development
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan visited China to discuss environmental education and training of "green" personnel. Agreements were reached to enhance collaboration between educational and research institutions. Memoranda of understanding were signed between Green University and Chinese counterparts for student/faculty exchange and joint research on satellite data for environmental monitoring.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia to Elevate Political Dialogue to Practical Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Serbia on September 7-8 to strengthen bilateral relations. The visit aims to transform existing political trust into concrete economic outcomes, including trade, investment, and logistical cooperation, building on recent diplomatic and economic engagement.

item.title: White House Website Features Anti-Immigrant Video Games
item.description: The White House website has launched anti-immigrant video games, drawing criticism from human rights advocates. One game involves catching migrants crossing the Rio Grande, while another simulates building a wall on the U.S.-Mexico border.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks third among central banks buying gold year-to-date
item.description: Despite selling nearly one ton of gold in July, Uzbekistan remains a major buyer, ranking third globally for net purchases since the start of the year, totaling 40 tons. Central banks worldwide increased reserves by 23 tons in July, with China and Poland being the largest buyers.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP appointed CIS IPA observer coordinator for Russian Duma elections
item.description: Gula Kozhokulova, a member of Kyrgyzstan's Jogorku Kenesh, has been appointed coordinator of international observers from the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly for the upcoming Russian State Duma elections. The observer group will include representatives from CIS parliaments and experts. The elections are scheduled for September 18-20, 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP Appointed CIS Election Observer Coordinator
item.description: Gula Kozhokulova, a member of the Jogorku Kenesh committee on international affairs, defense, security, and migration, has been appointed coordinator of international observers from the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly for Russia's State Duma elections. The observers will monitor the elections, scheduled for September 18-20, 2026, at the invitation of the State Duma chairman.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to export berries to China following phytosanitary protocol signing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and China have signed a phytosanitary protocol allowing the official export of fresh fruits and berries to China. Kyrgyz producers can now export raspberries, blackberries, and currants. The Ministry of Agriculture recommends specific high-yield varieties suitable for export.

item.title: Washington Governor congratulates Uzbekistan on opening first consulate in Seattle
item.description: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson congratulated Uzbekistan on the opening of its first consulate general in Seattle. He emphasized that the new diplomatic mission will create new opportunities for trade, investment, technology, innovation, education, and scientific research.

item.title: Kazakhstan Wins First Place in Team Standings at 2026 World Nomad Games
item.description: Kazakhstan secured first place in the team standings at the VI World Nomad Games held in Kyrgyzstan from August 31 to September 6, 2026. The games concluded successfully, showcasing strong competition and camaraderie between participating nations, particularly Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan in Kok Boru and Kok Bure.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan receives measuring transformers for electricity accounting
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has received 90 sets of measuring transformers as part of the "Modernization and Sustainable Development of the Electric Power Sector" project, funded by the World Bank. The equipment is intended for accurate electricity accounting and reliable operation of protection systems. Installation is planned by the end of October 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Receives Measuring Transformers for Electricity Metering
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has received 90 sets of measuring transformers as part of the "Modernization and Sustainable Development of the Electric Power Sector" project, funded by the World Bank. The equipment, costing 41.64 million soms, will be installed by the end of October 2026 to ensure accurate electricity accounting and reliable system protection.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Dollar exchange rate rises after three-day decline
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased following a three-day period of decline. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 8.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Increase Pensions by 20 Percent Starting October 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved a 20 percent increase for the insurance portion of pensions, effective October 1, 2026. The raise will range from 1,000 to 10,000 soms. This adjustment applies to pensions granted before October 2026, excluding the basic pension part. Minimum pension after recalculation will be 8,800 soms.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to increase pensions by 20% starting October 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers approved a 20% indexation of the insurance part of pensions, effective October 1, 2026. The increase will range from 1,000 to 10,000 soms. This applies to pensions granted before October 1, 2026, under the state social insurance law. The minimum total pension after recalculation will be 8,800 soms.

item.title: Kazakhstan Secures First Place in World Nomad Games Medal Standings After Recount
item.description: Following a recount, Kazakhstan has claimed first place in the medal standings at the VI World Nomad Games held in Kyrgyzstan. The organizing committee decided to count medals for three Kazakh athletes separately. Kyrgyzstan's presidential press secretary congratulated Kazakhstan, emphasizing that the Games fostered mutual respect and unity.

item.title: Gas extraction begins at new 'Patron' gas condensate field in Qashqadaryo region
item.description: Gas extraction has commenced at the new 'Patron' gas condensate field in the Mirishkor district of Uzbekistan's Qashqadaryo region. The first exploration well was connected to the gas pipeline on September 2. The Ministry of Energy refuted social media reports of a gas explosion, clarifying that the video showed the well's testing and commissioning process.

item.title: Uzbekistan to mandate state registration for medical professionals by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce state registration for medical and pharmaceutical workers. The system will be voluntary from 2027 to 2030 and mandatory thereafter. Unregistered specialists will be unable to practice medicine or pharmacy. A unified electronic registry will be created, integrating data on qualifications and professional activities.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia deepen bilateral ties, RTV reports
item.description: Serbian media outlet RTV highlighted the growing relationship between Uzbekistan and Serbia, encompassing political dialogue, inter-parliamentary ties, humanitarian cooperation, and trade-economic collaboration. The report noted that bilateral relations have reached a multi-faceted partnership level, built on mutual respect and national interest alignment.

item.title: Uzbekistan to reform medical and pharmaceutical training system
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its medical and pharmaceutical training system starting the 2027/2028 academic year. The six-year "General Medicine" bachelor's program will replace the current "Medical Practice" course. Graduates will undergo a year of practical training to become family doctors. Admission quotas will be based on regional needs and specialist shortages.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances judicial aid quality, increasing judge numbers significantly
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly improved judicial assistance quality by increasing the number of judges. From 1,057 judges for 32 million people in 2016, the number rose to 1,731 for 39 million people today. This reform created a unified court system and specialized administrative courts for challenging state actions.

item.title: Combating Poverty Requires Tailored Family-Based Solutions, Uzbek President States
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized that poverty reduction requires understanding each family's specific needs and providing targeted support, not just general aid. Addressing poverty effectively involves helping families start businesses, acquire skills, and secure stable incomes through their own labor, according to a recent meeting.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Company for Supplying Liquefied Gas to Population
item.description: A company will be established in Uzbekistan to supply liquefied gas to the population. Compensation will be provided for each kilogram of liquefied gas purchased by vulnerable social groups. Further details are available on daryo.uz.
